subject: Embeddings integration: post-call recap & next steps
messages:
From: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>
To: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Cc: platform@acme.com
Date: 2027-04-18T15:12:00-07:00
Subject: Follow-up: embeddings integration post-call

Thanks for the call today — appreciate the clear overview of Redwood's embeddings offering. A couple of follow-ups from our side as we scope the migration: 

- Current embeddings provider: VectorCloud (managed). Typical vector dims: 1024 for documents, 384 for short-form user queries.
- Monthly embed volume: ~4M docs (most historical), ~150k realtime queries.
- Current setup normalizes vectors to unit length; we do dense ANN on FAISS with IVF+PQ.

Key questions:
1) How disruptive is the migration to Redwood for our existing index format?
2) Recommended vector dimension for parity vs cost/latency? We want to avoid reindexing everything but are open if accuracy gains are material.
3) Suggested batching & normalization strategies (we see throughput issues at >2k items/batch).

Would love a short doc or checklist we can take to infra. Also, can we get a quick estimate of cost delta if we move docs->768-dim embeddings instead of 1024?

Thanks,
Jenna
Product Manager, ACME Corp

--
Attachment: acme-current-embeddings-stats.csv (csv, 42KB)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>

Cc: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-18T17:05:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: embeddings integration post-call

Thanks Jenna — great questions. Posting a short recap and next steps; Dev is looped for a brief technical checklist.

Recap / high-level guidance:
- Migration disruption: Redwood supports on-the-fly reindexing and compatibility with FAISS exports. If you can export IVF+PQ centroids and vectors we can provide a compatibility script to convert centroids and re-map indexes to Redwood's vector store. That said, we commonly advise a staged migration (read-only backfill -> hybrid reads -> cutover) to keep queries stable.

- Vector dims: 768 is a common sweet spot (good trade-off of cost/latency vs retrieval quality). Since you already have 1024 for documents, two paths:
  1) Keep 1024 for historical docs (no reindex) and serve queries with vector projection to 1024 on Redwood (higher cost).
  2) Re-embed historical docs to 768 and use a unified 768 pipeline (lower ongoing cost, one-time reindex expense).

- Batching & normalization:
  - We recommend batch sizes 512-2048 for offline backfills (depends on GPU memory and quantization). For realtime ingestion we commonly use 64-256 per batch to keep tail latency <100ms.
  - Normalization: unit-length normalization (L2) before indexing works well with cosine/inner-product similarity and is what your current pipeline uses — that's fully supported.

Next steps (proposal):
1) Dev to share a short tech checklist (export formats, vector sample, current index size) — see attached Redwood migration guide.
2) We run a quick eval: ingest a 10k sample into a sandbox Redwood instance and produce R@10/precision deltas between 1024 vs 768.
3) Based on eval, pick either "gradual re-embed" or "compatibility layer" approach and plan a rolling reindex.

Cost ballpark: switching documents from 1024->768 typically reduces storage & per-query cost ~25-30% depending on quantization. We'll follow up with a more exact delta after we see the sample.

Attachments: redwood-embeddings-migration-guide.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Senior Account Executive, Redwood Inference
marissa_cole@redwood.com

From: Dev Patel <dev_patel@redwood.com>
To: Jenna Park <jenna.park@acme.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa_cole@redwood.com>
Date: 2027-04-19T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: embeddings integration post-call

Hi Jenna — quick technical checklist and some sizing notes below. Happy to join a short follow-up if it helps.

Checklist (what we need from ACME):
- Sample export: 10k vectors (CSV/npz) + metadata (doc_id, created_at).
- FAISS export (if available): IVF centroids and PQ tables (this speeds compatibility migration).
- Peak batch sizes for ingestion and realtime SLA targets (p95 latency target).
- Typical query vector dims and encoder (OpenAI-similar / in-house model).

Sizing recommendations:
- For offline re-embedding (4M docs -> 768): plan for ~48-72 GPU-hours depending on encoder; parallelize across N instances. We provide orchestration scripts for this.
- For continuous realtime ingestion: set batching window to 100-200ms and batch size 64-256 depending on request pattern. This keeps the GPU KV cache hit rates high and keeps p99 <350ms in our experiments.
- For PQ/quantized indexes: using 8-bit or product quantization we'll reduce storage by ~4-8x with minimal impact if you fine-tune parameters (we can recommend params once we see a sample).

Structured output & reranker notes:
- If you plan to use structured tool-calling (e.g., search -> rerank -> tool call), we recommend returning the top K (K=50) dense results and running a light re-ranker model (e.g., cross-encoder at smaller sequence length) to produce a final ranked list. That limits expensive cross-encoder calls.
- Redwood supports routing queries based on model latency/cost profiles — you can route high-SLA search queries to higher-dim indexes or higher-performance instances.

Auth/SDK setup (quick):
- SDK: python/js clients support streaming ingest and bulk upload APIs. We'll provide a short snippet in the migration guide.
- Auth: API keys + optional per-team KMS-based signing if you need key isolation for production.

I'll attach a small script to project vectors into 768 using a lightweight PCA fallback if re-embedding is not immediately feasible (lossy but sometimes acceptable for quick evals).

Let me know when you can share the sample export and we'll spin up a sandbox.

-Dev
Senior Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
dev_patel@redwood.com

Attachments referenced: redwood-embeddings-migration-guide.pdf
